steps.text: Toss radishes with salt; let stand for about 10 minutes. Drain any liquid and transfer radishes to a large bowl; add red onion and cucumber slices.
Whisk olive oil, vinegar, dill, garlic, and sugar together in a small bowl until well mixed; pour over vegetables and toss to combine. Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Summer Radish Salad
raw_recipe.description: This gorgeous radish salad is easy to rustle up with sliced radishes, red onion, cucumber, and a garlic vinaigrette for a refreshing summer side dish.
raw_recipe.name: Summer Radish Salad

review.reviewBody: I went out and bought fresh radishes specifically for this salad. I only added some fresh ground pepper, no other changes. I made this when I got home from the store this morning and left it in the fridge for a couple hours before I scooped some out and ate it for lunch. This is the tastiest way I've eaten radishes, pretty much EVER. This salad is incredible. I'm about to go fix another bowl it's so good. WOW!

I had really high hopes for this salad but I have to disagree with al the people saying it was really good. Honestly all I could taste was olive oil. The "dressing" was olive oil with a hint of vinegar. I literally couldn't eat it. I might as well have been drinking olive oil out of the bottle. I think however if you made the dressing actually a vinaigrette instead of olive oil then this would be decent. I would also cut back on the onions as red onions are very strong and maybe add more cucumber. Also in terms of quantity there was just too much dressing compared to the ingredients. They were swimming in it.

I had some fresh radishes to use up. I really enjoyed this salad. I went a little heavier on the vinegar and used unseasoned rice vinegar instead of white vinegar and a little lighter on the olive oil. I also salted both the radishes and the cukes together. Added a bit of fresh ground black pepper at the end.
It was awesome. I added a juiced lemon, a little salt and extra vinegar to the dressing. Also, no sugar.

The ratio of oil to vinegar is way off on this dish. And it needs more seasoning with salt. I added white balsamic vinegar to make the ratio to oil almost equal plus more salt and it is good! I love using the radishes with the cucumbers and onions.
I put much less olive oil, I cut the red onion into small pieces and add some lemon juice and it was perfect.

I love this salad! Made a couple of changes to use what I had on hand. Used balsamic vinegar, lemon juice, fresh ground pepper, salt , Splenda instead of sugar, green onions instead of the red. Other ingredients left as the same in recipe. Incredibly delicious salad that I can see me making all summer long.

This is the most basic way you can make the salad. I would advise squeezing half of a lemon juice, a pinch of fresh garlic, sea salt and pepper, sub the sugar for honey...it’s DELISH that way. No need for olive oil ... just the cider vinegar is fine.

Good simple salad. I used a variety of fresh radishes from the local farm, cukes, and added a small amount of red pepper (my wife is not a fan of onion, especially raw onion) . I add some onion to my serving. No dill, so I used some basil. Very good.
Very similar to Asian cucumber salad, i used a little more than quarter cup of apple cider vinegar and only about 2 tbsp of olive oil. I used 2 cloves garlic and added black pepper.

I loved all the ingredients that go into this salad, however before pouring the dressing on to the vegetables I tasted it and was too bland. I added Balsamic Vinegar, Asian Vinegar, a little more sugar until I got the flavor I wanted. It was so yummy with this combo of flavors!!
Great way to use homegrown veggies! So convenient to have it already prepared in the fridge when you're ready to serve it! Thank you!

I agree with others who said this has waaaayy too much oil. I expected it to be like a light Asian salad dressing, with a balance of light vinegars, sweetness, and oil. It was drowning in the oil. I added some rice wine vinegar, lime juice, a bit more sugar and some salt and it's at least edible.
Added a half top honey

I have to agree with a previous review that it was WAY too much olive oil. Luckily I did not put all the olive oil dressing on the salad. It would have totally ruined it. If I make this again, I will use a favored bottled dressing, as I find most recipe dressings I don't like at all.
A simple and refreshing salad and as the title suggests, ideal for summer.
No changes. Always have lots of radishes and cukes on hand, so handy salad to make and tasty.
Myhusband wasn't that crazy about it. He said it was missing lime and salt! :D I had to leave out the salt because we follow a low sodium diet. I also used dry dill instead of fresh.
Used dried Dill because that's what I have. Used a mandolin for slicing it was quicker and consistent sliced !
Added garlic scapes, grape tomatoes & thinly sliced Vidalias. Excellent
